note: The structural matrix. One row per destination, one column per facet. Facets describe the EVENING; properties of her PEOPLE belong to the tone tiles and are measured in voice space, never here. Audited by scripts/audit-matrix.mjs — never quote a failure list from anywhere else.

facetNotes.schedule: posted = the invitation names the hours. anchored = one thing happens AT ITS HOUR and the rest finds its own (Westhampton's drinks hour, New Orleans' second wind at midnight). standing = the house's own unannounced rhythms — nothing is named, but the night has always gone this way (Nantucket, Côte d'Azur's eternal lunch). unplanned = nobody decided anything; it became a party. anchored and standing were briefly ONE level on the argument that a host cannot tell them apart. That was wrong, and the collision proved it: Westhampton/Nantucket failed on [dress, food] with no schedule contribution, which is impossible if those two houses keep time differently — and they do. A named hour and an unnamed habit are different answers to 'does anything happen at a time?'
facetNotes.starts: WHEN THE THING BEGINS, and only that — `ending` already answers how late it runs, and one facet cannot answer two questions (that is why `hour` was replaced by this in the contrast pass). FOUR LEVELS, AND THE FOURTH IS APPLICANT-SIDE ONLY. `late` was added when the hour question was ungated and reworded (db/037), because 'a late supper' is an hour a host can now name and morning/afternoon/evening had nowhere to put it. NO ROW HOLDS `late` AND NONE SHOULD BE MOVED TO IT: not one of the eighteen is authored as beginning at midnight, and re-declaring a cell to populate a level is fitting the evidence to the column. So the audit prints DEAD starts.late and that line is CORRECT — it is the catalogue saying, accurately, that the room which begins at one in the morning has not been written. See docs/proposals.md, 2026-08-23. The consequence for scoring is that the comparison is ASYMMETRIC — a member level against a row level, never row against row — and src/lib/selection/structure.ts holds the table and the argument. The rooms that ARE late-night are not reached through this facet at all; they are reached through `ending = until_morning`, which is a different claim and has its own question.
facetNotes.ending: WHAT KIND OF NIGHT IT IS, which is not the same claim as `starts` and must not be collapsed into it. `starts` records the hour she named; this records what she thinks a good evening does with its last hour. The split is what lets a Sunday lunch that goes until dark and a dinner that stops at eleven both be said. Levels sit 7 / 7 / 4 across the eighteen rows, the most even split any facet has, and the audit scores it second only to `schedule` for pairs separated. Fed since db/037 by `how_it_ends`, whose three options are the founder's own scenes and whose codes ARE these levels, so the answer resolves with no translation step.
facetNotes.size: Pure headcount. few = 8 or under. table = 8 to 16. crowd = 16 and over. "One long table" is EVIDENCE for the middle band, never the definition — the furniture fact stays in the prose.
facetNotes.spectacle: performed = A SHOW THE ROOM WATCHES — a floor show, cliff divers, the band that is the point. EXCLUSION, written here because it will otherwise creep: a toast, or a carving at the table, is CEREMONY and not spectacle. The room attending to one person it knows is not an audience.

fedBy.note: WHICH QUIZ ANSWER SUPPLIES EACH COLUMN. CLAUDE.md rule 15: nothing grades that does not prune, and every instrument traces to a supplier. This block is that trace, as data rather than as a claim in a comment, so that src/lib/selection/structure.ts can rank on exactly the fed facets and a test can assert the two lists are the same list. THREE STATES, and `field: null` covers the last two — an unfed column is one nothing supplies, and a column supplied by a hardcoded default identical for every applicant is the same thing wearing a number. An entry here is a promise that a HOST STATES THIS LEVEL, not that a level could be guessed from something she said: a veto ('a schedule that runs the day') is negative evidence about one level and does not state a cell, and a fact about her guests is not a fact about the evening. Reading a level out of an answer that meant something else is the retro-tagging failure this catalogue exists to escape (rule 3), so the honest entry for seven of the nine is null with the reason written down. THE RANKER IS DRIVEN BY THIS BLOCK. Adding a supplier is an entry here plus a bridge row in a migration; it is deliberately not a code change, so the column count the reveal claims can never drift from the column count it uses.

arrival.why: UNFED. No question asks how people come through the door. `assigned` is Catskills alone and is a fingerprint level, which makes this the most delicate of the seven to wire: a single question reaching it would name a room in one tap. Wiring it needs a scene question in the idiom of `how_it_ends`, not a tag borrowed from somewhere else.

schedule.why: UNFED. The nearest answer is `anti_preferences/schedule` — 'a schedule that runs the day' — and it is a VETO. It says one level is unwanted; it does not say which of the remaining three the evening is, and `anchored` against `standing` is precisely the distinction it cannot make (see facetNotes). Negative evidence about one level is not a stated cell. It is also the facet carrying the most separation in the audit, which makes it the strongest candidate for the next question and the worst one to fake.

volume.why: UNFED. `anti_preferences/loud` vetoes one end and `group_fun` describes HER PEOPLE, which rule 1 forbids as a source for a cell about the evening. docs/destination-contrasts.md keeps this facet on the argument that size and hour genuinely constrain it — that is an argument for the facet existing, not evidence of which level a given host is at.

dress.why: FED by db/070. Two options, asked of everyone, no activeWhen. The option codes ARE these levels, so the bridge is an identity and there is no translation to get wrong — the same property `how_it_ends` has and the hour does not. THE ENTRY THIS REPLACED said `group_fun/dress_up` is 'commit to an outfit', which is a thing her people enjoy rather than a rule this evening has (rule 14, kept): that reading was correct and is the reason this is a NEW QUESTION rather than a bridge onto an existing tile. Bridging `dress_up` would have broken rule 1 — a guest property travels unchanged to every party they attend — and would have DOUBLE-COUNTED, since those tiles already feed the tone vector. Founder, 2026-09-06: "Dress — 'this evening, jackets or not.' Weakest separator, most legible question, not group_fun/dress_up (that is her people)." Weakest is right and is why it went first: 84 of 190 pairs, eighth of nine, two levels, one screen — the cheap one, proving the wiring before `schedule`.

food.why: UNFED, and it looks fed, which is why it is written out. `how_made` is an axis of EFFORT — actually made / half made / bought and arranged — and this facet is an axis of PROVENANCE, and they come apart at both ends: `arrived` (Tahiti alone) is not a rung on the making ladder, and `half_made` names no level here. `food_plan` says whether there is a table, not who cooked. Mapping either onto this column would be inventing a cell out of an answer about something else.

ending.why: FED by db/037. Three options, asked of everyone, no activeWhen. The option codes ARE these levels, so the bridge is an identity and there is no translation to get wrong.

starts.why: FED by db/037, through a SECOND resolution of an answer that already had one. The same four codes resolve to `meal_shape` for the composed table and to `evening_start` for this column — brunch to morning, lunch to afternoon, dinner to evening, a late supper to `late`. Before db/037 the question was gated behind `food_plan = sit_down`, so a cocktail party, a booked restaurant and a drinks-only evening stated no hour anywhere and this column was ranked against a fallback for all three.

size.why: UNFED, and the closest of the seven to being wireable. `guest_count_band` is arithmetic and this facet is pure headcount, so a bridge is available — but the bands and the levels do not line up: `from_13_to_20` straddles the 16 that divides `one_table` from `crowd`, and picking a side is a judgement rather than a translation. It is also a scale answer, which docs/destination-contrasts.md holds to a different stage on purpose ('guest count and spend are likewise filters, not taste'), so wiring it into a ranker is a decision about the seam and not only about a boundary.

spectacle.why: UNFED. `group_fun/perform` is 'sing, badly, on purpose', which is her people volunteering — and the facet's own exclusion note says the room attending to one person it knows is CEREMONY and not spectacle. The two are near-opposites. Claimed by two rooms of eighteen, so the fingerprint risk is the same one `arrival` has.

rejectedFacets.acquaintance: Varies per event, so it passes the evening test, but it does not constrain WHICH WORLD FITS. A constraint that governs assembly, not a ranker.
rejectedFacets.cuisine: Eleven levels for sixteen rooms, seven of which reach exactly one room. Not a facet — a destination picker, and it memorises an answer key derived from the destinations in the first place.
rejectedFacets.audience: Dropped, and the stated reason was WRONG. It was rejected because only six destinations carry a reply convention, so a permeability facet could not be derived for the other six. But EVERY destination carries a populated `voice.audience` field, which states the guest relation directly and is the better evidence class — Portofino's 'the few of us who came, who have all met before' against New Orleans' 'everybody coming, which is more people than were asked'. The wrong field was checked. NOT resurrected: the matrix is clean at nine facets and a tenth column would now solve a problem that no longer exists. But `voice.audience` is the evidence to use if permeability is ever needed, and it is what carried the Portofino/Cote d'Azur twin case.

twinRule.statement: A room may sit below the gate against EXACTLY ONE other room — its twin — provided all four conditions hold.
conditions: distance >= 1. Zero is not a twin, it is one room written twice.
voice affinity < 0.65. The pair must be separable by the OTHER instrument; the tiebreak has to have something to work with.
the pair is DECLARED here as a tiebreak pair. An undeclared sub-gate pair is a failure, not a twin.
ONE TWIN PER ROOM. A room with two sub-gate partners cannot twin with either — that is a crowded corner, not a pair.
twinRule.why: Havana/New Orleans is the precedent instance and the reason the rule exists: the same night in shape, separated by 'nobody in the house is the target' against 'everybody is fair game', at 0.172 in voice space. Forcing a structural facet between them would smuggle a guest property back into the matrix. The twin rule says so out loud instead.

Closed against open. The lexicons say it twice — `between us` against `come up: the road is the answer and nobody is counted`.
